title: Punch a card's two filing holes on their marks
instruction: Punch the card's two filing holes on their marks.
context: Two-hole filing (ISO 838) puts the holes 80 mm apart and 12 mm in from the edge; a page punched off its marks sits out of line with the others in the binder. Punching handouts, planner pages and recipe cards for a ring binder is an everyday office, school and home job.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the table top: x forward, y to the robot's left. A dark green cutting mat (28 x 30 cm, 2 mm) under everything, centred (21, 0). Desk two-hole punch, fixed to the table: black painted steel base x 24.5-30, y -11 to 11, its bed 2.0 cm above the table; a 6 mm throat facing the robot, front face at x 26.2; two 6 mm round punches 80 mm apart at x 27.0, y -4 and +4, over dies with an open chip cavity below; a back stop 12 mm behind the punches (x 28.2); a white centre line on the bed at y 0. Steel lever (2 cm wide, 6 mm thick) pivoted behind the punches at (29.5, 9), 5.5 cm above the table, reaching forward over the punch head to a red handle knob at x 19.5-22.5, y 8-12.5; pressing the knob about 3 cm drives the punches 9 mm, and a return spring lifts them. A stock equivalent is the Rapesco 835-P metal two-hole lever punch (two 6 mm holes 80 mm apart, 40-sheet capacity, about GBP 13-25), fixed to the table, with a centre line marked on its bed and, if its throat is deeper, a back stop fitted 12 mm behind the punches. Grey foam stand x 9.5-24.5, y -14.5 to 7.8, 2.0 cm tall, level with the bed. Card: yellow A6 card stock (300 g/m2, 148 x 105 mm, 4.7 g) lying flat on the stand, one long edge facing the punch; two black crosshair marks 12 mm in from that edge, 80 mm apart, each printed as two 0.8 mm lines 30 mm long (the line toward the edge stops 1 mm short of it), so the lines stay visible around a punched hole. Nominal start: card centred (18.5, -2.0), square to the punch, its edge 44.5 mm short of the stop. Each trial moves it by a random x offset of -0.8 to +0.8 cm, y offset of -1.2 to +1.2 cm and turn of -10 to +10 degrees (uniform, drawn from the trial seed; the screenshot shows the start drawn for seed 0: 3.3 mm forward, 11.1 mm to the robot's right, turned 6.3 degrees anticlockwise seen from above). Arms at READY.
scoring: Scored from the card. A hole counts when the punch has gone through the card with the hole's centre within 1.5 mm of its mark; a hole more than 1.5 mm from its mark does not count. 1.0: both holes, held 1 s (the trial ends there); otherwise 0.5 for one or two holes (two before the 1 s hold is complete) and 0.0 for none, at the end. Real trial: punch a fresh card, then measure each hole's centre from the centre of its crosshair (where its lines would cross) with a steel rule; a photo with a scale also works. Simulation: each hole is a 6 mm disc pre-scored at its mark that the punch must push down through the card against a 30 N cutting resistance. It is cut free only when it has been pushed the card's full thickness and the punch tip is 0.5 mm below the card's underside, with the disc's centre within 1.5 mm of the punch's axis and the card on the bed (not raised more than 0.5 mm above it); it counts once it has fallen out of the card into the die. Pressing with no card, with the card short of the punches, off its marks or raised off the bed, or stopping the press with the punches on or in the card, frees nothing.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; card modelled 1.5 mm thick (real 0.35 mm). Each hole is a 6 mm disc on a slide that resists the punch with up to 30 N, an estimate for shear-ground punch tips (README); measured, 65 N on the punch head does not cut, 70 N cuts both. Tips and discs collide as square prisms of similar area; discs weigh 10 g in the model so tips cannot sink through. The sim card can sink up to 1.5 mm into the bed under load; the release check allows that. 500 N/m return spring; punch fixed to table.
reset_notes: Each trial uses a fresh pre-marked card (a punched card cannot be reused). Empty the chip cavity. Lay the card on the foam stand at the nominal start (centre at (18.5, -2.0), square to the punch, edge 44.5 mm short of the stop), then move it by the trial's random offsets and turn (for example drawn with a random number generator from the ranges in the setup), measured with a ruler and a protractor.
